sample_unit: chest imaging cases (each read by 10 readers, 1000 reader-case pairs per session)

links.outcome: Reader adequate interaction and overreliance with versus without LLM assistance, by LLM accuracy and confidence
links.effect: Model confidence (OR 3.82) and reader expertise (OR 2.06) independently associated with adequate interaction; higher rationale quality increased acceptance of incorrect suggestions (OR 1.71) while reducing rejection of correct ones (OR 0.79).
links.quote: Higher rationale quality reduced rejection of correct suggestions (OR, 0.79 [95% CI: 0.67, 0.93]; P = .005) but increased acceptance of incorrect suggestions (OR, 1.71 [95% CI: 1.47, 1.99]; P < .001).

links.outcome: Reader acceptance of incorrect LLM suggestions (automation bias/overreliance)
links.effect: Higher rationale quality increased acceptance of incorrect suggestions (OR 1.71); higher reader expertise (OR 0.54) and reader confidence (OR 0.80) reduced acceptance of incorrect suggestions.
links.quote: Higher reader expertise (OR, 0.54 [95% CI: 0.41, 0.70]; P < .001) and reader confidence (OR, 0.80 [95% CI: 0.67, 0.94]; P = .007) were protective, reducing acceptance of incorrect suggestions.

links.outcome: Association of model confidence with readers' adequate acceptance or rejection of LLM suggestions
links.effect: Model confidence associated with adequate interaction (OR 3.82, 95% CI 1.58-9.25), with weaker effect among experts (OR 0.79).
links.quote: After multivariable adjustment, model confidence (odds ratio [OR], 3.82 [95% CI: 1.58, 9.25]; P = .003) and reader expertise (OR, 2.06 [95% CI: 1.38, 3.07]; P < .001) were independently associated with adequate interaction, with a weaker effect of confidence among experts (OR, 0.79 [95% CI: 0.67, 0.94]; P = .008).

unlisted_practices: Effect of LLM rationale quality on reader uptake of correct versus incorrect suggestions

screen.reason: Evaluates reader-LLM interaction (clinician review of LLM advice) across different levels of model confidence, rationale presentation, and reader expertise in a multireader offline study.

primary.practice: human-AI collaboration with model confidence scores and rationale provision
